newsitem.title: MEXICO: Carso will maintain good growth - Slim.
newsitem.headline: Carso will maintain good growth - Slim.

text.p: Mexican holding company Grupo Carso will continue to turn in high margins and healthy growth even if it does not expand as aggressively as in the past, according to company chairman Carlos Slim.
"Carso is doing very well...the industrial group still has a lot of growth left in it," Slim told a group of foreign reporters on Wednesday.
Carso is a conglomerate made up of cigarette company Cigatam, industrial firm Condumex, mining firms Frisco and Nacobre, retailer Sanborns and tire company Corporacion Llantera.
It recently spun off Carso Global Telecom from the rest of the firm.

Slim said Carso could not be accused of being passive given its recent purchases of shares in telephone company Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex). Slim said Carso Global Telecom now holds 19 percent of Telmex. But he added that, if Carso has been more conservative recently, it was due to financial considerations: "We wanted to watch Carso's debt levels during the crisis, to ensure that it had a healthy balance sheet."
Carso, one of Mexico's most diversified holding companies, saw excellent operating results during last November, according to Slim.
Carso grew quickly in the early 1990s under the guidance of the billionaire Slim, who gained a reputation for buying up undervalued companies and turning them around for big profits.
Some financial analysts have wondered where Carso's future growth would come from given its mature business mix.
Slim said Sanborns is mulling opening outlets in the United States and said Condumex was studying investments in Brazil. He would not go into details.
